title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels
abstract: arXiv:2611.23035v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value scaled by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding on one quarter of its dimensions. The Gemma 4 report states that this design reduces the global KV cache by up to 37.5%, but the open serving engines that we checked still store a full key and a full value: 1,024 values per KV head and token. We store one 640-value row instead, exact in real arithmetic, and an unchanged paged attention kernel reads it through two overlapping strided views as its key cache and its value cache. In a vLLM prototype with the 16-bit 31B model, the outputs are bit-identical to an emulation of the same arithmetic on the stock cache, 2 of 432 final answers differ from the stock engine (within its run-to-run noise), and the steady decode KV memory per request falls by a factor of 1.34 to 1.40 at 32K to 64K tokens. translated_title: The K=V Cache of Gemma 4 Only Needs to Be Stored Once: Achieving Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine Without Modifying the Attention Kernel
translated_abstract: In the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B, the value is the normalized key projection, and the key is the value multiplied by a fixed weight, with rotary position encoding applied to only one quarter of its dimensions. The Gemma 4 technical report points out that this design can reduce the global KV cache by up to 37.5%, but the open-source serving engines we inspected still store a complete key and a complete value: 1024 values per KV head per token. We instead store only one row of 640 values, which is exact in real-number arithmetic, and an unmodified paged attention kernel reads it as its key cache and value cache through two overlapping strided views. In a vLLM prototype using the 16-bit 31B model, the outputs are bit-identical to an emulation of the same arithmetic on the original cache; 2 of 432 final answers differ from the original engine (within its run-to-run noise range); and at 32K to 64K tokens, the steady decoding KV memory per request decreases by a factor of 1.34 to 1.40. tldr: This paper exploits the linear dependence between the key and value in the global attention layers of Gemma 4 31B (K=V), storing only one 640-value row without modifying the attention kernel, which reads the key and value caches through two overlapping strided views, achieving a 1.34 to 1.40 fold reduction in KV cache memory during decoding with bit-identical outputs.
en_tdlr: This paper exploits the linear K=V dependence in Gemma 4 31B's global attention layers by storing a single 640-value row that an unmodified paged attention kernel reads as both key and value caches through two overlapping strided views, cutting decode KV memory by 1.34–1.40x with bit-identical outputs.
